translation: The hang bone (胻骨) is the bone of the lower leg below the knee and above the ankle, commonly called the lianjing bone (臁脛骨). Its bones are two roots; the one in front is called the cheng bone (成骨), also called the gan bone (骭骨), and its form is thick; the one behind is called the auxiliary bone (輔骨), and its form is thin, also commonly called the laotang bone (勞堂骨). If it is injured by a fall or blow, and the tip of the bone protrudes obliquely outward, the flesh is broken and blood flows without stopping, with pain and groaning in a thin voice, and food and drink are taken little; if the person moreover has always had weak qi and blood, it must lead to danger and death.
